content.title: About
content.content: Manhattan clam chowder is a thick, creamy soup made with milk and cream, featuring clams, potatoes, onions, carrots, and celery. The recipe originated in early 20th‑century New York and became popular for its rich flavor and velvety texture.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Unlike New England chowder, Manhattan chowder is prepared on a dairy base rather than a tomato base.
The earliest documented recipe dates to 1911 and appeared in New York culinary magazines.
The soup was often served in upscale seafood restaurants in the 1920s, regarded as a high‑class dish.
Traditionally fresh clams are used, but mass‑produced versions frequently rely on canned clams.
A common variation adds smoked bacon to enhance the smoky aroma.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Clams provide easily digestible protein that supports tissue repair and maintenance.

items.title: Source of vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 is essential for nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron from the seafood helps maintain healthy hemoglobin levels.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Small amounts of omega‑3s contribute to heart health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: Vitamin D
items.content: The creamy base supplies vitamin D, important for bone health and immunity.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Clams can trigger severe allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Cream and butter make the soup calorie‑dense; portion control is advised for weight management.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Canned clams often contain added salt, which may be problematic for hypertension.

items.title: Food poisoning risk
items.content: Improperly stored clams can harbor bacteria that cause foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the soup hot, typically with croutons, fresh herbs, or crisp bacon bits. A squeeze of lemon juice can brighten the flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. When frozen, it can be stored for up to 2 months after cooling and portioning.
